correctness.rationale: Every subset in either height-two order is convex. The seven disjoint cardinality/diagonal classes are exhaustive and each five-statistic tuple is computed from ambient predecessors/successors. The binomial formula follows by labelled counting. Statistical agreement holds iff both selected levels have at least two elements, or one has at least two and the other is empty, or both are empty, yielding exactly (2^n-n)^2. The distinguished coefficient n versus zero follows from the incomparable diagonal pairs. A separate direct relation enumeration verified all coefficients through n=7, the agreement law through n=8 and formula identities through n=100; these finite checks do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The dimension-n standard examples provide a canonical non-series-parallel test family for the new five-statistic polynomial. The formula determines its entire joint distribution and quantifies an exact robustness phenomenon under removal of n order-relations: (2^n-n)^2 signatures remain identical while a specific coefficient changes from zero to n. The result is not the trivial total convex-subset count or a substitution into the published ordinal-sum formula.
